interface.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: desktop product design concept for Dispatch, an agent collaboration application.
Primary request: Show an elegant, practical agent configuration interface that separates a reusable agent definition from a project assignment. This is a proposed design, not a screenshot of implemented software.
Composition: large high-resolution landscape canvas approximately 2400 x 1600, flat straight-on application screen, crisp legible typography. All numbered groups 1 through 10 must be visible and readable. No device frame. Use Dispatch's established navy narrow icon rail, pale blue-gray agent sidebar, white workspace, dark navy headings, restrained teal primary buttons, Inter-like sans-serif. Thin borders, compact well-spaced fields, no gradients or decorative illustrations.
Layout: 56px rail at left; slim sidebar titled "Agents" with "+ New agent", Recovery Engineer selected, Archivist, Evidence Reviewer, Developer. Main editor uses a spacious two-column grid of numbered sections 1–9. Right-hand assignment drawer takes about 27% of screen and is visually separated from the reusable form. The main area is headed "Recovery Engineer" with breadcrumb "Agents / Edit definition", a small amber "Design proposal" badge, and subtitle "Reusable expertise, connected to a project when needed". Bottom editor bar "Cancel" and teal "Save revision". The assignment drawer has its own "Add to project" button.

Exact numbered groups and content:
1 "Identity" — Name field "Recovery Engineer"; Description field "Inspect old backups and recover verifiable files."; small read-only "Revision 3 · Draft changes".
2 "Instructions" — one large textarea with four concise labeled paragraphs: "Purpose: Recover valuable files from old storage."; "Method: Inventory, inspect, verify, preserve provenance."; "Deliverables: Recovery manifest and unresolved gaps."; "Collaboration: Ask Archivist to classify; Reviewer to verify." Text above says "Reusable role, method, output standard, and collaboration rules".
3 "Model" — Provider select "OpenAI"; Model select "GPT-6 Astra"; Thinking select "High".
4 "Capabilities" — small amber "Proposed controls"; "Extensions" chips "Archive inspection" and "Evidence tools"; "Tools" chips "List" "Inspect" "Extract" "Verify". Caption "Select installed capabilities".
5 "Knowledge & memory" — small amber "Proposed"; "Sources" field "Knowledge library"; "Procedures" field "Archive recovery guide"; "Memory" select "Evidence ledger + wiki".
6 "Connections & identity" — status card "Recovery storage" with "Identity: Recovery service account"; subtle lock icon and label "Operator managed"; helper "Access is enforced by the connected service".
7 "Execution" — small amber "Proposed"; "Runner" select "Managed worker"; "Workspace" select "Per conversation".
8 "Long-running work" — small amber "Proposed"; "Workflow" select "Recover archive"; helper "Inventory → Inspect → Reconcile".
9 "Qualification" — small amber "Proposed"; "Readiness check" select "Recovery smoke case"; neutral text "Not run"; button "Run check".

Right drawer numbered 10 "Project assignment" with amber "Proposed" badge and subtitle "Specific to this project". Fields: "Project" select "Home Photos"; "Goal" multiline "Find photos, email archives, and other useful old files."; "Inputs" chip "Existing inventory + restored objects"; "Output location" field "Project evidence ledger"; "Collaborators" chips "Archivist" "Evidence Reviewer"; "Constraints" field "Preserve originals; cite source locations."; "Agent revision" read-only "Revision 3". Bottom helper "One definition can serve many projects." and teal "Add to project".

Constraints: numbers 1–10 are small consistent teal circular annotation badges placed beside each section heading, meant to match a companion technical graphic. Show all controls with comfortable readable spacing. The main editor and project assignment are separate save operations. Do not include SQLite/code paths in this product UI. Do not imply that new fields are already implemented. No copied real credentials, URLs, account information, photos, or chat history.
interface.correction: Use case: text-localization. Edit this UI mockup with one exact correction: in numbered section 5, change the misspelled label "Sourcer" to "Sources". Keep every other word, number, field, value, layout, color, size, and visual element unchanged. Preserve the entire full-resolution image and opaque white/pale background. This is a precision text correction only.

explainer.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: technical companion graphic for a Dispatch agent-configuration UI.
Primary request: Precisely explain where each numbered UI field goes in Pi Durable, distinguishing SQLite data from executable code and clearly marking proposed additions.
Style: clean professional technical editorial infographic, portrait canvas, high resolution and exceptionally legible text. White background, navy headings, teal numbered badges 1–10 matching the UI, blue current labels, amber dashed boxes for PROPOSED, gray code panels. Crisp sans-serif, monospaced identifiers. No decorative robots. Prioritize exact technical spelling.
Title: "From agent fields to Pi Durable"
Subtitle: "Dispatch proposal · verified against Pi Durable 1.0.1"
Top principle, prominent: "Saved configuration selects behavior. Registered code implements it."

Top storage panel:
Heading "The actual SQLite file: <stateDir>/pi.sqlite"
Two connected boxes:
"documents" — "Identity + address" — "id, kind, scope_kind, owner_id, record"
arrow labeled "documents.id = document_revisions.document_id"
"document_revisions" — "JSON values + changes" — "content, kind, version, seq"
Small explanatory line: "Read latest base + later deltas. documents.record is metadata, not the field values."
Below, a compact two-item key:
"D = dispatch.catalog / session scope (owner_id 0) / agents[]"
"A = pi.agent / conversation scope (owner_id = conversation ID)"
"Paths below refer to materialized JSON values. * means proposed, not implemented."

Center: ten-row numbered mapping table, 3 columns "UI FIELDS" | "SAVED DATA" | "RUNTIME CONCEPT".
Use enough height for all ten rows. Exact row content:
1 "Identity — name, description, revision" | "D.name · D.description · D.revision" | "Reusable Dispatch definition; revision pinned to participant"
2 "Instructions — purpose, method, deliverables, collaboration" | "D.instructions → A.instructions" | "One text field; combined with extension sections; rendered prompt → entries (pi.system)"
3 "Model — provider, model, thinking" | "D.provider + D.modelId → A.model; D.thinkingLevel → A.thinkingLevel" | "Per-conversation model configuration"
4 "Capabilities — extensions, tools" | "D.extensions + D.tools → A.extensions + A.tools" | "Names are saved. Registry resolves executable tools, sections, hooks, wrappers, tasks. New selectors proposed."
5 "Knowledge — sources, procedures, memory" | "D.profile*: knowledgeRefs, procedureRefs, memoryPolicy" | "Proposed retrieval tools + prompt sections; links do not ingest content automatically"
6 "Connections — service, identity" | "agent-connections.json; dispatch.mcp-bindings; dispatch.mcp-catalog" | "Operator config outside DB; bindings + cached discovery in DB; service enforces access"
7 "Execution — runner, workspace" | "D.profile*: runtimeProfileId, workspacePolicy; A.cwd" | "Host resolves ExecutionEnv; cwd is a path, not a sandbox"
8 "Long-running work — workflow" | "D.profile*.workflowId; tasks.record: state.checkpoint" | "Registered defineTask code + native durable task state; workflow picker proposed"
9 "Qualification — readiness check, result" | "D.profile*.qualificationId; dispatch.qualification* results" | "Proposed check definition + execution + recorded result"
10 "Project assignment — project, goal, inputs, output, collaborators, constraints, revision" | "dispatch.assignment* / conversation scope" | "Proposed: projectId, goal, inputRefs, outputRef, collaboratorIds, constraints, agentDefinitionId, agentRevision"

Bottom panel split in two:
"IN SQLITE" — "Definitions, selected names, instructions, binding IDs, task checkpoints, transcript entries, custom document values."
"OUTSIDE SQLITE" — "Extension implementations, tool servers, ExecutionEnv code, credentials, source files and recovered artifacts. Store references to large artifacts."
Small closing flow:
"Save definition → choose revision → create conversation → configure pi.agent → run registered behavior"
Legend at bottom: "Blue: existing storage concepts · Amber *: proposed schema or controls · Gray: code / external resources"
Constraints: exact technical identifiers, no invented native agents table, no claim executable extension code is serialized into SQLite, no suggestion instructions enforce permissions, no unsupported claim of automatic project-assignment execution or automatic memory. All ten numbered rows must be present. Keep the physical storage explanation and per-field map equally readable. You may wrap text within rows. Do not include irrelevant product navigation.
